user.text: Navigating from home to the product page is slow. Make the product title appear immediately while the live inventory loads.

history.assistant:
The build passes and confirms the fix works. The route table shows the key result: - /product is now marked ◐ (Partial Prerender) — "prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content" Previously the page was a single Server Component that awaited getInventory() at the top level, so the entire route (including the static

Premium Widget

title) was blocked until inventory resolved. Now: 1. app/product/page.tsx — renders the static title immediately as a synchronous Server Component. 2. app/product/inventory.tsx — a separate async Server Component that awaits getInventory(). 3. — wraps the inventory so Next.js streams the title shell first, then fills in the live inventory when it resolves (showing "Loading inventory…" in the meantime). With Partial Prerender enabled (Next.js 16 default), the static title is prerendered and served instantly during navigation, while the dynamic inventory streams in afterward.

I found the issue. `app/product/page.tsx` is a Server Component that `await`s `getInventory()` at the top level. The entire product route is blocked until inventory resolves, so nothing renders during navigation. The fix is to split the static title into the page (which streams immediately) and move the live inventory into a separate async Server Component that suspends independently.
